analysis:
This is a CI-only change: runner moves, opt-in threat review, docs and a changelog. No provider runtime, wire protocol, key custody or attestation code changed, so the provider threat-model assets and threats (T-041 etc.) are not affected.

threat-model-review.yml: `pull_request_target` now fires only on `labeled`, and the job runs only for `run-threat-model`. Adding a label requires triage or write access, which is a narrower trigger than before. The scanner is still checked out from the default branch with `persist-credentials: false`, so untrusted PR code is not executed. `issues: write` is added only to delete the one-shot label; it is a small permission growth on a job that already has contents and pull-requests write. The 75s coalesce sleep and the draft check were removed. The one concern is the skipped-job-as-green behavior under clearance mode, reported as a finding. I could not verify whether `threat-review-gate.py` or the branch ruleset compensates for it; that code is outside the supplied evidence.

release-provider.yml: resolve-env, the qualify-sdk aggregate job, stage-release and publish-release moved from Blacksmith Linux to GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04`. These jobs handle R2 credentials and RELEASE_KEY (A-005). Hosted runners are ephemeral, and the pinned-hash tool install and the artifact id/digest-verified download are unchanged. I identified no regression, but the change in runner trust domain for secret-bearing jobs is worth a human acknowledgement. A 90-minute timeout was added to the signing job. The excerpt of lines 1065-1497 shows the signing, publication identity and digest-pinned flow unchanged.

Some files (release-provider.yml lines other than 1065-1497) were seen only as patch excerpts.

docs/developer/build.md and the changelog are documentation only. They describe other workflows (ci-dev, ci-master, darkbloom-route, watchdog) that are not in this batch; those need review in their own batch.

findings.detail: Head line 71 gates the `review` job on `github.event.label.name == 'run-threat-model'`, while the workflow still fires on every `labeled` event (line 6). Any other label added to a PR creates a run in which the `review` job is skipped. A skipped job reports as a passing check on that head SHA. The base workflow had a comment (base lines 70-71) saying clearance mode must not let a skipped success replace a failed required run. When `THREAT_REVIEW_REQUIRE_CLEARANCE=='true'`, a triager or any label-capable actor who adds an unrelated label (e.g. `bug`) after a failed or incomplete review can leave a skipped, green check on the same SHA. That would bypass the `threat-review-gate.py after` evaluation. The base `edited`-event carve-out was dropped without a clearance-mode equivalent. Fix: run the job in clearance mode regardless of label, or add a lightweight job that fails or stays pending until the gate has evaluated the head SHA. Alternatively, trigger only through a dedicated label-filtered mechanism that does not emit a required-check conclusion for other labels.
findings.title: Label-gated threat review job skips on unrelated labels, which can satisfy a required clearance check
